chapter_title: The Explanation of the Peace, what it is; the Right Hand; the Kiss; the Salutation.
chapter_note: The chapter opens with a clear dialogue-question frame, then presents a largely self-contained cosmological archetype: five “signs/mysteries” enacted in the descent/ascent of the First Man (peace, right hand, kiss, salutation, laying on of hands). Mid-chapter the editor repeatedly pivots from archetype to human social ritual (“in the midst of mankind”, “here and now”, “today”), producing multiple MIXED paragraphs. The second half shows strong editorial fatigue: institutional church initiation sequence, exhortation, and clerical authority material dominate. One paragraph contains a likely biblical/psalmic quotation about sitting at the right hand/footstool, treated as OVERLAY inside an otherwise cosmological unit (handled as MIXED with the citation removed).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic Q&A frame: disciples question the apostle; sets up topic in ritual terms. This is editorial apparatus, not substrate exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: So, these five signs are the mystery of the First Man. He came forth with them from the aeon of light. Also, when he finished his contest, he went up with these good signs. They received him into the aeons of light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution and self-referential revelatory/applied setup: “Then he says to his disciples… miniatures… I am the one who can reveal to you…”. These are compilation-frame and application-to-world cues, not the oldest impersonal teaching voice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core kernel identifies the five signs as primordial mysteries of the First Man’s descent/ascent (cosmic-structural). Surrounding sentences are personal disclosure + ‘displayed in the world’ application, indicating later editorial mediation.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.38⟩ The first peace is the one that the gods and the angels in the land of light gave to the First Man; when he comes out against the enemy. The gods and the angels were walking with him; escorting him, giving to him their peace and power, and their blessing and fortification. This is the first peace that the gods and the angels gave to the First Man; as he comes forth from the aeon of light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological narration establishing an archetype within the Light realm (gods/angels/aeon of light) without institutional targeting.

paragraphs.core_text: The first right hand is the one that the Mother of Life gave to the First Man; when he comes out to the contest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Compact archetypal mapping: divine being (Mother of Life) → action/sign given to First Man, entirely within cosmological system.

paragraphs.core_text: The first kiss is this one with which the Mother of Life embraced the First Man; as he separates from her, coming down to the contest. Even all the gods and the angels who are in the aeons of light were making to embrace him! [ ... ] all of them also, and the church tutelaries (?), and the kinsfolk who belong to the household of his people. They were making to embrace him as [he] separates from them, accompanying him out, embracing him with the kiss of affection and love.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic household scene; despite the translator’s uncertain gloss “church tutelaries (?)”, the passage functions as intra-plērōmatic kinship/escort imagery, not church-institution instruction.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.39⟩ The first salutation is the salutation with which the First Man made obeisance; when he comes out [to the depths] below. He was bending his knees, making obeisance to the God of truth, and all the aeons [of light] who belong to the household of his people; entreating them for a power to escort him, as he comes forth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Archetypal obeisance described within the Light household; no ‘today/in the church’ pivot.

paragraphs.core_text: The first laying on of hands is the one that the Mother of Life bequeathed upon the head of the First Man. She armed him and made him mighty. She laid hands on him, and sent him to the battle. He descended. He completed his struggle with the great powers and the enmity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic mechanism (arming/sending/struggle) presented as cosmic process; not a rule for the community.

paragraphs.core_text: By the [se] five signs and these five myst[e]ri[es] the First Man came forth from the aeons of light against the enemy. He humbled him. He was victorious against him by them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative statement closing the first archetypal cycle; entirely cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, when he ascended from the war, he came in to the kingdom of the household of his people by these five mysteries!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completion of the descent/ascent arc; no later institutional anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: The peace with which [he ascen]ded is the peace that the summons gave to him, [w]hen it was sent forth from the [Fa]ther of Life. It gave him the peace in the world of darkness. Also, that peace with which he descended is th[e sam]e as the one with which he ascended from the struggle!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the application-to-present pivot: “Therefore… did this peace here and now come about… among the powers of the Father.” This crosses from archetype to contemporary ritual legitimation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins with cosmological causation (Summons from Father of Life; peace in world of darkness), then turns to ‘here and now’ etiology of human practice—classic archetype→social application seam.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this second right hand is the one that the Living Spirit gave the First Man, when he [brou]ght him upward out from the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ‘appropriate to the mystery… occurs in the midst of mankind…’ application clause, which maps the archetype onto human greeting practice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clean archetypal identification (Living Spirit → right hand) followed by explicit mankind-application in the full paragraph.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, this second kiss is the one with which the [Father o]f Life and the Mother of the living embraced the First Man, when he ascended from the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the explicit social/experiential application: “Again, this kiss occurs among mankind… go away from home… approach one another…”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic embrace is core; the paragraph’s second half is an editor using it to explain ordinary human leave-taking/meeting customs.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.40⟩ [The] second salutation with which the First Man made obeisance [ ... this] time to the God of truth and [ ... ] the blessed aeons and al[l] the aeons [ ... the] whole [land] of light, whe[n] the Father of Life and the Mother of the living brought the Man upward from the abyss of the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the present-tense legitimation of contemporary custom: “Appropriate to the mystery… this one that occurs today in the midst of mankind…”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Archetypal obeisance upon restoration to the Light is core; ‘today… in the midst of mankind’ is an editorial anchor to contemporary ritual.

paragraphs.core_text: The second laying on of hands is this: When the Living Spirit brought the First Man upward from the war, he saved him from all the surging waves. He brought him upward, he gave him ease in the great aeons of light, which belong to the household of his people. He set [him] firmly before the Father, the Lord of the totality. He received this great laying on of hands that he may become leader of his brethren in the new aeon.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed a likely biblical/psalmic citation embedded as direct speech (“…sit at my right hand… footstool…”), plus the concluding archetype→mankind application (“Again, appropriate to the mystery… occurs in the midst of mankind…”). The citation is OVERLAY material; the application is later institutional/ritual legitimation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmology (Living Spirit rescues/sets First Man before the Father) is interrupted by a recognizable ‘right hand/footstool’ scriptural voice, indicating later Judeo-Christian overlay insertion.

paragraphs.core_text: These five mysteries and these five signs came about first in the divine. Mankind has been taught them; and they have instituted them in their midst [ ... but] these mysteries were not at the beginning amongst the powers of darkness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the specific mediation claim “They were proclaimed in this world by an apostle.” The term “apostle” functions as compilation/church-historical framing rather than substrate exposition.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The cosmic priority claim (‘first in the divine’ / ‘not at the beginning among Darkness’) fits core origin discourse, while apostolic proclamation is a later legitimating frame.
Archetype is redirected to institutional election: “choose his church.” This is cosmos→church/institution mapping, characteristic of later pastoral extension.
Stepwise church initiation sequence (peace → child of peace → elected → right hand → approach church). Institutional catechesis rather than cosmological substrate.
Explicit ‘holy church’ and moral-programmatic elements (“good works”); not cosmic-system exposition.
Community-building promises tied to receiving ritual signs; although ‘Light Mind’ appears, the paragraph functions as institutional formation/assurance, not primordial cosmology.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again: At the time of their coming forth, the Light Form shall come forth before them; and she redeems them from the darkness to the light [ ... ] This Light Form calms the person, with the kiss and her quiet, from fear of the demons w[ho de]stroy his body. By her asp[ec]t and her image [the] heart of the elect one, who is come forth from his bo[d]y, shall be calm for [him]. Afterwards, the angel who h[o]lds the victory prize extends to him the right hand. And it draws him out of the abyss of his body, and accepts him in with the [k]iss and love. That soul shall make obeisance to its red[eem]er, who is this Light Form. And also, at the inst[ant when ... ] he shall be perfected and increased according to [ ... / ... ] in the household of the living ones, with the go[ds] and the angel[s]. [An]d he receives the crown [ ... ] glory in the life for ever.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional/hagiographic add-on phrase “and all the apostles and the chosen,” which imports church-role terminology into an otherwise cosmological afterlife scene.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Predominantly cosmological eschatology (Light Form, demons, angel with prize, ascent to household of living ones). A small late intrusion uses ‘apostles/chosen’ language, suggesting secondary church colouring.
Direct exhortation and audience address (“my brethren and my limbs… let you…”), plus self-authorization (“Father who sent me”): application voice typical of late homiletic/pastoral layer.
Fragmentary but oriented to hearers’ benefit (“you may part from the world… you have understood…”). Not impersonal cosmological exposition.
Explicit clerical hierarchy (teachers/deacons/presbyters), obedience, and sin for rejecting laying on of hands—institutional enforcement layer.
Second-person exhortation (“my beloved ones, hasten… listen…”) and moral providential assurances; late application material, heavily lacunose.
